analysis.title: Europe Open - AI'nt looking good
key_insights: Asia equities fell sharply overnight after US equities had their worst day since April 2025 (Liberation Day). Kospi -6%, Nikkei -5%, Taiex -4.5%, HK/China stocks down about -1%.

Nasdaq futures are +0.8% and SPX e-minis flat at print despite the Asia selloff. Citi's Asia strategist expects intraday bounces in e-minis to be sold and a test of 7100, a level that has held since the start of AI. A failure there would carry more negative implications.
Asia strategist view: markets are at 'fair' value but not yet 'cheap'. Citi expects a round of cuts to excessively optimistic earnings estimates.
Concern about Democratic wins in data center states, which could bring data center moratoriums, is in the foreground. State-level regulation would not be enacted until next year.
No flight to quality overnight. USTs are calm, USD is slightly higher, and CHF and JPY are slightly weaker (JPY -0.2%, CHF flat).

Market participants are waiting for US NFP. Average hourly earnings is the key measure, and softer trends would limit a hawkish reaction to headline payrolls. Citi expects NFP +65k, consensus is 70k, whisper 82k (a later section cites 75k). Citi expects AHE +0.3% MoM and unemployment at 4.2%.

Rates desk: positioning is tactically long duration, and payrolls need to validate the growth concern for duration to extend cleanly. Desk flows show tentative steepening in futures and SOFR bull steepeners. JGB front end was the best performer, with yields +15bp.
Brent is close to returning to $100 and the oil pickup is not helping risk. Gold is down -1% overnight, with the $4000 level holding.
Trump met Russia's presidential envoy and predicted a 'big agreement' that 'might involve all of Europe', which is a constructive Russia/Ukraine headline.
FX vols rose significantly in AUDUSD, NZDUSD and USDCNH, but activity was quiet into NFP and focused on intraweek contracts. The options trader says positioning is light and 25bps is priced for NFP.
NZ general election on Saturday is polling very tight. Labour intends to restore the RBNZ dual mandate of inflation and employment. Citi expects no more RBNZ moves this year.

Citi Global Macro Strategy: the POLLS signal is working and suggests staying out of US equities until late November. Four 'Generals' are below the 200-day moving average, and the 'Generals' signal is close to triggering. Citi sees no typical post-midterm year-end rally and buys a far out-of-the-money receiver swaption in case the AI bubble has burst.

Citi European Rates Weekly: energy prices would need to fall significantly to derail further ECB/BoE hikes. A second MPC hike could come as soon as December, so Citi enters Dec/Feb MPC SONIA flatteners.
Citi European Rates also argues ad-hoc LTROs could be a second line of defence for monetary policy transmission after Schnabel's speech, and recommends buying Schatz spreads.

Canada labor report: Citi expects employment -5k in October versus consensus of 15k, with unemployment at 6.5%. Downside surprises would support no more BoC hikes this year and cuts resuming next year.
Germany industrial production printed +0.7% MoM, above consensus but down from 1.4% prior.
